paraphrase: Persons are to be known as of three kinds — lesser, middling and supreme. Whoever by whatever means seeks only the happiness of saṃsāra for their own sake is the lesser person. Whoever turns their back on the pleasures of existence, turns away from harmful deeds, and seeks only their own peace is the middling person. Whoever, through the suffering belonging to their own continuum, wholly wishes for the complete ending of all the suffering of others is the supreme person.

paraphrase: Before the protectors I generate the mind of complete awakening, invite all beings as my guests and will free them from saṃsāra. From now until I reach supreme awakening I shall not harbour harmful intent, anger, avarice or envy. I shall live in pure conduct, abandon wrongdoing and desire, and with joy in the vow of ethics train following the Buddhas. I shall not be eager to reach awakening quickly for myself, but remain to the end of time for the sake of even a single being. I shall purify immeasurable, inconceivable fields and remain in the ten directions for those who call my name; I shall purify all actions of body and speech, and of mind, and not do non-virtuous deeds.

paraphrase: It is not reasonable for an existent to arise; a non-existent, like a sky-flower, does not arise either; both faults would follow for 'both', so both together do not arise either. Things do not arise from themselves, nor from others, nor from both, nor without a cause — therefore they are without own-nature by essence. Or else, when all phenomena are analysed as one or many, no own-nature is found, and so it is certain they are without own-nature.

paraphrase: This existence arisen from conceptualization has conceptualization as its nature; therefore the abandoning of all conceptualization is supreme nirvāṇa. So the Blessed One said that conceptualization is great ignorance, which makes one fall into the ocean of saṃsāra; abiding in non-conceptual concentration, the non-conceptual is clear like the sky. The Dhāraṇī of Entering the Non-conceptual also says that a son of the Conqueror who reflects on the non-conceptual in this dharma passes beyond conceptualizations hard to cross and gradually attains the non-conceptual. Having ascertained by scripture and reasoning that all phenomena are unborn and without own-nature, meditate without conceptualization.

paraphrase: If one wishes to complete the accumulations for awakening easily, through the activities of pacifying, increasing and the rest accomplished by the power of mantra, and through the power of the eight great accomplishments such as the good vase, and wishes to practise the secret mantra taught in the action, performance and other tantras, then, to receive the master's empowerment, one should please the holy teacher with service, gifts of jewels and the like, and by doing whatever he says. By pleasing the teacher and receiving the complete master's empowerment, one is purified of all wrongdoing and becomes fit to accomplish the siddhis.
